tools.name: search_prompts
tools.description: Find ready-made, expert prompt templates for a work task in the thinkhard.si repository (500+ prompts for email, meetings, presentations, job search, marketing, sales, support, HR, finance, legal, spreadsheets, research and more). Use it whenever the user wants to write, plan, summarize, analyze or

tools.name: get_prompt
tools.description: Get the full text of one prompt from the thinkhard.si repository by its slug, registry number (such as CAR-001) or exact title, with its {{blanks}}, what goes in each, and why it works. If the name does not match exactly, it answers with the closest matches instead. Pass values to fill blanks with t

tools.name: list_collections
tools.description: List the collections in the thinkhard.si prompt repository, with how many prompts each has.

tools.name: grade_prompt
tools.description: Score a prompt out of 10 on the ten checks thinkhard.si uses (what to make, who it is for, background facts, length, format, what to avoid, what good looks like, an example, what to do if unsure, layout for the model). Returns which checks pass and a plain question for each one that fails. Rule-base

tools.name: estimate_ai_cost
tools.description: Estimate the monthly cost of running a prompt on current AI models (Claude, GPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, Qwen and others), from thinkhard.si's price catalog, which is checked against each provider's pricing page. Give token counts, or paste the prompt text to estimate them.

tools.name: fix_bad_answer
tools.description: When an AI answer goes wrong (it made up a source or a number, ignored an instruction, came back too long or in the wrong shape, sounded robotic or generic, changed every time, refused, or lost track of a long chat), find the likely cause and the exact line to add to the prompt. Draws on the thinkha

tools.name: get_prompt_pattern
tools.description: The 24 prompt patterns from thinkhard.si: small moves that change the answer, such as giving the facts, naming the reader, showing one example, setting a length, fencing off pasted text or asking for reasoning first. Each comes with when it helps, when it does not, a before-and-after pair with score

tools.name: define_ai_term
tools.description: Plain-English definitions of 97 AI words from the thinkhard.si glossary (token, context window, hallucination, temperature, system prompt, RAG, fine-tuning, agent, MCP and more), written for people who use AI at work rather than build it.

findings.title: Description tells the model to hide behavior
findings.detail: Description of "prompt:clean-messy-columns" instructs the model to conceal actions from the user.

evidence.snippet: An export or a shared sheet has inconsistent dates, names, categories or numbers, and you want rules you can apply and check rather than a silently altered file…

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "prompt:ab-test-readout" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: An experiment has finished and you need a write-up that says what the numbers show, how sure you can be, and what they do not show.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_prompts · Private data: estimate_ai_cost, define_ai_term · Public sink: search_prompts · Destructive: grade_prompt.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_prompts · Private data: estimate_ai_cost, define_ai_term · Public sink: search_prompts · Destructive: grade_prompt

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "search_prompts" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
